A service must declare its validations in a Validations partial.

Back to STX rulesRead The Standard source

What The Standard says

A service must declare its validations in a Validations partial. The analyser reports this as a warning at the declaration or statement that needs attention.

Why it matters

This rule belongs to the The Standard family. Following it keeps responsibilities and intent visible to readers, tooling and future maintainers.

Bad code example

// Violates STX0008: A service must declare its validations in a Validations partial.
// StudentService.cs
internal partial class StudentService(IStudentBroker studentBroker)
    : IStudentService
{
    public ValueTask<Student> AddStudentAsync(Student newStudent) =>
        TryCatch<Student>(operation: async () =>
        {
            await ValidateStudentOnAdd(newStudent);
            await studentBroker.InsertStudentAsync(newStudent: newStudent);

            return newStudent;
        });

    private static ValueTask ValidateStudentOnAdd(Student newStudent)
    {
        ValidationRulesEngine.Validate(inputs: newStudent);

        return ValueTask.CompletedTask;
    }
}

Good code example

// Follows STX0008
// StudentService.cs
internal partial class StudentService(IStudentBroker studentBroker)
    : IStudentService
{
    public ValueTask<Student> AddStudentAsync(Student newStudent) =>
        TryCatch<Student>(operation: async () =>
        {
            await ValidateStudentOnAdd(newStudent);
            await studentBroker.InsertStudentAsync(newStudent: newStudent);

            return newStudent;
        });
}

// StudentService.Validations.cs
internal partial class StudentService
{
    private static ValueTask ValidateStudentOnAdd(Student newStudent)
    {
        ValidationRulesEngine.Validate(inputs: newStudent);

        return ValueTask.CompletedTask;
    }
}
